reason: Duplicate of the formula in T2-01 (same 'without distortion, denial, modality, likening'), in the context of the hadith of God's descent; kept as a reserve passage about the Sunni 'middle' between Jahmiyya and anthropomorphists (text: 'فهم وسط في باب صفات الله سبحانه وتعالى: بين أهل التعطيل الجهمية وأهل التمثيل المشبهة').

Second version of the 'without distortion/denial/modality/likening' formula in his own voice ('ومذهب السلف أنهم يصفون الله بما وصف به نفسه...'). Duplicate of T2-01/T2-02; seen in search output, not read in full.

Quotation of a creed by another author (attribution not established in the extract; the section is a series of 'ونعتقد...' statements introduced by 'قال'). Contains 'القرآن كلام الله ليس بمخلوق ولا حال في مخلوق'. Needs the quoted author identified before any use.
Quotation of Salaf narrations (Walid ibn Muslim reporting Malik, Sufyan al-Thawri, al-Layth, al-Awza'i: 'أمروها كما جاءت بلا كيف'). Reported material; used only as context for T2-03.

Relevant to the 'parts' question: 'صفاتنا منها ما هي أعيان وأجسام، وهي أبعاض لنا، كالوجه واليد' (our attributes like face and hand are parts for us, not for God). Limit reached; strong candidate for the orchestrator (question 2).
His circularity critique of the composition argument (the 'dur' point: 'فلا يجوز أن تجعلوا هذا دليلا على نفي التركيب'). Limit reached; candidate for question 2.

Mainly reports the philosophers' list of forbidden compositions (genus-differentia, essence-attribute, matter-form, existence-quiddity, etc.) and their argument. Opponent's view; shows the full list of 'tarkib' types. Not used (reports opponents).

Says the dispute among Sunni scholars over 'God's speech subsisting in Him' is verbal and that the imams agreed it is uncreated; also names Ibn Kullab. Good candidate for the Word-as-attribute question (theme T); limit reached.
Describes sects and states 'جمهور المسلمين يقولون: إن القرآن العربي كلام الله وقد تكلم الله به بحرف وصوت'. Candidate for theme T; limit reached.
Report of the Karramiyya view (uncreated Qur'an spoken 'with letters and sound', but 'created' events in God). Reports an opponent group.

Quotes a Jahmi formula ('if God spoke to Moses, speech needs letters and sound, which are created') and gives his answer in three parts. The answer is his, but the passage starts with an opponent's quotation; candidate for theme T, limit reached.

Reports a classification of names into three kinds (the same as the object, other than it, or 'neither it nor other' - e.g. 'al-'Alim', 'al-Qadir'), attributed to the Ash'ari and his followers. Opponent's view; relevant only to the wording of question 4.

Christian-side: says the Christians' triad terms (Father, Son, Holy Spirit) are not in the Prophets' books and that the claim that the triad expresses life and speech is not what the words mean. C theme; limit reached. Candidate for the C team.

Reports a Christian apologist's defence ('Yahya ibn 'Adi'): 'Zayd the doctor, the calculator and the writer' analogy for hypostases, and his critique. C theme; a named Christian author (Yahya ibn 'Adi) whose text could be checked. Candidate for the C team.

Earlier part of the same passage used in T2-08 (he says a flat yes or no to 'is God's speech letters and sound?' is an error and reports the Kullabi and 'letters and sound' views). Used as context, not as a separate passage.
